offence_severity: 3 years to life imprisonment and fine
physical_harm: Threat to cause death or hurt
number_of_offences: Eight persons indicted; six finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found premeditation/planning as part of the conspiracy to extract ransom
motive: Extracting ransom under threat to the life of the victim
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of victim as a whole was truthful - His elaborate testimony not only projected the stage-wise developments following his abduction till his release, the same remained unshaken substantially even by his cross-examination - Evidence adduced vis-a-vis the stage-wise recovery of the currency notes, fire-arms, the Honda City car etc. from the successive disclosures made by the accused persons also established their complicity in the offence
witness_credibility: The victim's testimony was found to be truthful and unshaken by cross-examination. His detailed account of the abduction and ransom process was corroborated by other evidence, including the recovery of items and the statements of his father and other witnesses.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 09.01.2008; Trial judgment: 21.04.2014; High Court decision: 21.04.2014; Supreme Court decision: 21.11.2016
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Subromaniam Prasad, R. Basant, Himanshu Gupta, Arun Poomulli, Anil Kumar Tandale; Counsel for the State: V. Madhukar, Ms. Anvita Cowshish, Ms. Lubna Naaz, Kuldip Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction upheld; High Court: Conviction upheld; Supreme Court: Appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the evidence of the victim was truthful and detailed, establishing the complicity of the accused in the abduction and ransom plot. The victim's testimony, along with the recovery of items like currency notes, firearms, and the Honda City car from the accused, supported the prosecution's case. The call details, though challenged, were not essential to proving the charges against the accused.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the victim's failure to name the appellant at the initial stage and the omission of the investigating agency to hold the TIP (Taluka Police Inspector) were fatal to the prosecution case. They also claimed that the victim's identification of the appellant at trial was insufficient and that the call details were inadmissible, undermining the prosecution's evidence.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that conspiracy requires an act (actus reus) and a mental state (mens rea). It emphasized that conspirators do not need to know all details of the plot, but must be co-participants in the main object, with unity of purpose and participation at different stages.
precedent_relied_upon: Anvar P. V. v. P.K. Basheer and others 2014 (11) SCR 399; Pullukuri Kotajya and others v. King Emperror AIR 1947 PC 67; Bodhraj @ Bodha and Others v. State of Jammu & Kashmir 2002 (2) Suppl. SCR 67; Ferozuddin Basheeruddin and Others v. State of Kerala (2001)7 SCC 596; Mir Nagvi Askari v. Central Bureau of Investigation 2009 (13) SCR 124; Mohd. Amin v. CBI 2008 (16) SCR 155
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution proved the charges levelled against the appellants beyond reasonable doubt, including the conspiracy and abduction for ransom. The courts below correctly analyzed the evidence, and the Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with the conviction and sentence.
